svg.text: ClaimSense AI × AutoSure Insurance — architecture AS BUILT (through M4 step 5, prompt m2-v13)

Every arrow is a labelled data flow (B1–B20, legend below). Blue = deterministic code · Orange = model judgment · Green = human · Grey = systems/data · Purple = operations. Solid border = deployed on AWS · dashed border = runs locally in containers. Synthetic data only.
HUMAN — a licensed adjuster is accountable for every outcome (confirm is human-only)
DETERMINISTIC CODE — identity · access · dates · money · risk indicators (never a model)
MODEL JUDGMENT — five typed agents; every judgment cites its evidence
DETERMINISTIC CODE — THE GOVERNED DOOR (MCP 2025-06-18 + REST), the only path to client systems
SYSTEMS OF RECORD (synthetic mocks) · AWS DATA SERVICES
reads only claims assigned to her
Adjuster Console — CloudFront → ALB → ECS Fargate
Streamlit · Cognito sign-in · queue · Ask ClaimSense
citations ⊆ retrieved · PII mask · second opinion
THE DOOR — API Gateway (Cognito JWT authorizer; /mcp: door verifies the delegated token) → Lambda (container image) · same image runs locally
auth before routing · grants.json deny-by-default · entitled() = group + assigned adjuster · REST 403 · idempotency · retry/breaker · audit EVERY call
OpenAI key + demo sign-in → task role
live gate ≥ 90% · push THE tested build
Adjuster signs in at Cognito (local: dev issuer); the ID token carries user + groups to the console.
Console sends claim_id + token to the orchestrator; the door re-checks the token on every call.
Locally, Keycloak performs the RFC 8693 exchange (D-041); on AWS the door's /oauth/token does it (D-039).
Before any agent: the door checks the grant and entitlement. Refused → no agent runs, $0, audit row.
Door → systems of record: get_claim, list/get documents, get_policy (typed, granted, audited).
Orchestrator → agents in a fixed order ①→②→③→④; inputs PII-masked, untrusted text wrapped as data.
Agents ↔ OpenAI API: masked prompts out, strict structured outputs back (pinned model snapshots).
Coverage's search_clauses → the door → the KB; unprovenanced chunks are quarantined (G2) at the door.
DecisionCard → guardrails: code overwrites computed fields, checks citations, forces confirmation.
create_recommendation (Idempotency-Key) → a draft; escalations → SIU ticket / Slack via the door.
The card appears in the console: computed vs judgment, fraud indicators, verdict_source labelled.
Human-only confirm/override at the door; agent identities can never confirm (NEVER_DELEGATED).
Door → SIU ticketing: create_escalation_ticket (idempotent, retried with backoff, breaker).
Ticketing → door: HMAC-signed webhooks (5-min window, deduped by event_id, ordered by seq).
notify_oncall: a Slack page with a link, never claim data (granted, idempotent, audited).
On AWS the door reads the KB corpus, policies and documents from S3 (read-only role); manifest stays in
Every call, granted or refused, writes one append-only audit row (DynamoDB on AWS; /state locally).
The same rows as AUDIT lines in CloudWatch Logs, plus the API Gateway access log for edge 401s (D-042).
GitHub Actions: build once, live LLM gate ≥ 90% inside that image, then push THE tested build to ECR.
Secrets Manager / env: the OpenAI key reaches the orchestrator only; the door never holds a model key.
